headline: eBay beat on Q3 as GMV rose 16% FX-neutral, helped by Depop and collectibles; full-year outlook raised.
guidance_note: FY26 non-GAAP EPS raised to $6.25-6.30, revenue $12.62-12.67bn, GMV $91.5-91.9bn; Q4 GMV $23.7-24.1bn (+12-14% FX-neutral, ~4 pts Depop).
key_messages: GMV $23.2bn, +15% reported / +16% FX-neutral; Depop (closed Jul 30) added nearly 3 pts, so organic growth was ~13%.
US GMV ~$12.55bn (+27%) vs international ~$10.62bn (+4%), per a Zacks summary; international growth driven by UK and German focus categories/C2C.
Active buyers 147M including acquisitions; 136M organic, up just 1% YoY. US active buyers +6% organic (+13% pro forma with Depop).
Focus-category GMV +24%, led by collectibles, Motors, fashion and refurbished; management expects trading-card growth to moderate.
Advertising revenue $607M; GAAP EPS fell 13% to $1.11 while non-GAAP EPS rose 12%; ~9% staff cut announced Oct 20.

consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary enthusiast categories (collectibles, Motors parts, fashion, refurbished) grew broadly; no explicit macro caution found.
consumer.quote: eBay's strong third quarter results reflect continued momentum across our business priorities and customer segments as more consumers embrace recommerce. (CEO Jamie Iannone, via press coverage)

macro_read: Strong spend on collectibles and secondhand goods points to resilient discretionary demand from enthusiasts, while flat organic buyer counts show eBay's growth comes from deeper spend by existing buyers rather than a broad consumer surge.
notes: Depop acquisition (closed Jul 30, 2026) inflates growth: nearly 3 pts of FX-neutral GMV growth per CFO; one source said ~2.5 pts guided.
Revenue is the release's rounded headline ($3.2bn); exact figure not confirmed.
US/international GMV split comes from a Zacks summary, not verified against the release.
Restructuring (~9% of staff, per Oct 20 8-K coverage) charges mostly fall in Q4 2026 GAAP results.
Stock reaction: shares rose ~4.7% after hours; regular-session close on Oct 29 not confirmed, so left null.
No Q3 2026 management comments on tariffs/de minimis were found.
